financials.period: Statement dated 2026-08-06 covering the following twelve months
financials.stated_by: Beyond Meat management; existing cash and anticipated operating cash flows expected to cover requirements, conditional on revenue, cost and working-capital assumptions; not an independently calculated runway

debt_events.summary: Entered agreements to exchange approximately USD 15 million principal of 2027 convertible notes for common shares at 96% of face value. This was a debt-for-equity exchange, not new cash financing.
Following the September exchange, USD 14.5 million principal of 2027 notes remained outstanding, maturing 2027-03-15; disclosed on 2026-11-04.

Amended the 2030-note indenture to remove certain restrictions on repurchasing or exchanging 2027 notes for cash or equity. Extended the conversion interest make-whole period end from 2028-10-15 to 2029-01-15.

Reported covenant compliance under the term loan and 2030 notes, including USD 15 million minimum-liquidity requirements. During the first six months of 2026, holders converted USD 68.8 million principal of 2030 notes into shares; those notes permit 9.5% payment-in-kind interest instead of 7% cash interest.

Remedied a reporting-covenant default after failing to deliver audited annual financial statements to its lender by 2026-03-31. Filing the annual report and delivering accompanying documents restored compliance; this disclosure concerned a reporting default, not a missed debt payment.

Historical restructuring, outside the latest twelve-month window: completed an exchange cancelling USD 1,120,541,000 of 2027 notes for USD 209,721,000 of 2030 notes and 317,834,446 pre-reverse-split shares. The annual report classified it as a troubled debt restructuring because the company experienced financial difficulties and creditors granted concessions.

payment_behaviour.summary: The First Circuit docket records Sonate's appeal in the trademark litigation. This establishes continuing litigation, not payment delinquency or satisfaction of the judgment.

Court entered a USD 15,437,500 trademark-infringement judgment against Beyond Meat, reduced from the original jury award. The company disclosed it on 2026-09-22; payment or satisfaction was not verified.

Historical, disputed trade-payment evidence: Food Dive reported Creditsafe data indicating 36% of 2024 vendor bills were at least 91 days overdue. Beyond Meat rejected the figures as highly inaccurate. This is not evidence of current 2026 arrears.

distress_signals.summary: Filed a late-filing notice for the quarter ended 2026-09-26, citing unfinished close procedures involving impairments and lease modifications. Expected filing by 2026-11-10 but warned of further delay. The latest Form 10-Q verified in this review covers 2026-06-27; newer financial figures above come from the earnings release.
For the quarter ended 2026-09-26, revenue declined 8.1% year over year and operating results included USD 57.1 million of noncash long-lived-asset impairments.

Interim Chief Transformation Officer John Boken was scheduled to step down, with responsibilities transferred to the new full-time COO and other leaders. The filing describes a planned handover rather than an unexplained departure.

Quarterly filing reported unremediated material weaknesses in complex-transaction accounting and inventory valuation as of 2026-06-27. It also reported that the China operational wind-down was substantially complete during the first half of 2026.

Deloitte issued an unmodified financial-statement opinion but an adverse opinion on internal control over financial reporting because of material weaknesses. These are distinct opinions; the controls finding is not a going-concern qualification.

Historical workforce reduction: management approved approximately 40 North American layoffs, around 5% of the global workforce. The annual report says this reduction was substantially completed by the end of the third quarter of 2025.

ownership.value: Publicly listed company; Nasdaq ticker BYND.

output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-11-10, continuing losses, the historical troubled debt restructuring and the cured reporting-covenant default indicate weak internally generated debt-service capacity (financials; debt_events dated 2025-10-30 and 2026-04-09). Near-term payment risk is mitigated by USD 154.6 million of unrestricted cash versus USD 14.5 million of remaining 2027 notes, although operating cash burn continues (financials and debt_events as of 2026-09-26). The delayed quarterly filing, unremediated accounting controls and trademark judgment support elevated counterparty risk, without establishing imminent insolvency or current supplier-payment default (distress_signals and payment_behaviour).
